findings.reason: PyOpenCL Device objects do not provide a 'pci_domain_id_nv' attribute under the Khronos 'cl_nv_device_attribute_query' extension (which only defines CL_DEVICE_PCI_BUS_ID_NV and CL_DEVICE_PCI_SLOT_ID_NV). Direct attribute access raises an AttributeError, which is caught by line 182's bare 'except Exception:', silently falling through to 'EPHEMERAL_RUNTIME_ID'. Consequently, multiple physical NVIDIA GPUs without 'cl_khr_pci_bus_info' are incorrectly rejected as ambiguous by select_devices() (lines 280-282).

findings.reason: The acceptance specification (items 6 and 10) mandates corrupting the real activation at the first vendor boundary. Line 458 checks 'layer_owner[i] != layer_owner[i + 1]', which detects any device/context boundary rather than a vendor boundary. When more than two devices are selected and the first two devices share a vendor (e.g. two NVIDIA cards followed by AMD), corruption is mistakenly injected at an intra-vendor boundary instead of the vendor boundary. Furthermore, multi-GPU same-vendor selections will incorrectly execute corruption despite having no vendor boundary.

missing_qualification: NVIDIA physical PCI identity resolution under cl_nv_device_attribute_query fails with AttributeError on pci_domain_id_nv, degrading to EPHEMERAL_RUNTIME_ID and preventing multi-NVIDIA hardware discrimination.
First vendor-boundary corruption check compares runtime device IDs instead of vendor keys, corrupting intra-vendor boundaries in multi-card homogeneous prefix topologies.
Device discovery lacks discrimination for AMD PCIe topology (cl_amd_device_attribute_query) when cl_khr_pci_bus_info is absent, treating distinct AMD physical cards as ephemeral.
